findingMessages.p0004-correctness-mask-id-truncation: Mask ids from command/MCP params are narrowed with `v as u32`, which wraps instead of rejecting. `mask.delete {id: 4294967297}` (2^32+1) resolves to mask id 1 and deletes (or renames/inverts/moves via the same mask_id helper) a different, existing mask than the caller named, instead of returning `no mask 4294967297`. mask.select (line 545) likewise selects an unrelated mask. This contradicts the repository rule that input-derived numbers are hostile and must use checked conversion.
findingMessages.p0004-correctness-placenames-nonatomic-r: The download's own contract (line 183) says the new place-name files replace the old ones only when complete, but each file is written in place with std::fs::write (truncate then write). If the disk fills or the app quits while writing the ~cities file (line 204), the previously working gazetteer is replaced by a truncated one. metadata.placeNamesStatus then reports `downloaded: true` (it only checks the file exists), and Fill Location from GPS silently finds fewer or no places. The optional files are also written (line 199) before the cities file, so a failure there leaves a mix of old and new data.
findingMessages.p0004-correctness-staging-filename-colli: Downloads::start only refuses a second download of the same model id; different models download side by side into one shared staging folder keyed only by spec.file_name. Catalog entries (catalog.json) derive file_name from the URL basename and fall back to `model.onnx`, so two catalog models can share a name and write the same `.downloads/<name>.part`. Concurrently, they corrupt each other's partial file and both fail. If one finishes and the second starts before the next faces.pump, the second fetch reuses or overwrites `<name>`. finish_downloads installs the first id with `verified: true` and its recorded sha (no rehash, face_models.rs:265). That can install the other model's bytes under the first model's manifest, or leave the first job's Done path pointing at a file that is gone.
findingMessages.p0004-correctness-rename-start-overflow: photo.rename / photo.renamePreview take `start` as any u64 and cast it with `as usize`, with no upper bound. plan_rename_core iterates `(start..).zip(photos)`. With start = 18446744073709551615, RangeFrom::next overflows on the first step. In debug builds that panics: the command fails through the catch_unwind net rather than with a bad-params error. In release builds the sequence wraps to 0, 1, …. On 32-bit wasm, the `as usize` cast also silently truncates the value. This breaks the project's never-crash rule for hostile numeric input.
